statusText: The CME weekend halt still governs this assessment: nothing has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and nothing will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about six hours past the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail is 11% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green, because a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting. What changed this hour is the character of the Iran thread rather than its temperature. Last hour the US-Iran channel could be described as stalled; this hour Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi has said directly that "No negotiations have been held between us and the United States at this time" and that Tehran has not decided whether to resume them, while Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi put the blockade on an explicit condition - "This strait will only be opened and closed under Iran's command, and as long as you do not accept the reality of defeat and stop indulging in delusions, Iran will continue to enforce the blockade" - adding that the waterway "cannot be seized with a tweet, nor with an aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order." Against that, the 60-day negotiating window opened by June's memorandum of understanding expires on Monday with minimal direct contact having taken place. An empty channel with a dated expiry is a materially different object from a stalled one, and the physical evidence matches it: only two vessels transited the strait on Friday with no visible crude against a 130-140 peacetime norm, a bulk carrier was struck by an unknown projectile, and the ADNOC-linked hit reported today is the third such incident inside 48 hours. Stress therefore rises two points to 58% (elevated). The counterweights are unchanged and equally observed: VIX closed Friday at 14.25, less than a point above its 52-week low of 13.38, the Nasdaq-100 closed down only 0.13%, and a senior White House official has said Trump was joking about declaring Hormuz US territory. Confidence is 62% (solid): NQ futures, VIX and both crude benchmarks were re-read directly this hour and three independent geopolitical primaries corroborated the Iranian statements and the negotiating-window expiry; the 2-year and 10-year yields and the seven-day calendar are carried forward from earlier direct reads because a Friday close and a set of dated releases cannot change over a weekend.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (11%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. That reopen now carries an extra load, because it is the last liquid session before the June memorandum's 60-day negotiating window lapses on Monday with, on Araghchi's own account, no talks having taken place. Gap risk remains genuinely two-way. Pulling one way: an Iranian position that has moved from conditions-for-reopening to blockade-until-defeat, a negotiating window expiring into an empty channel, a Lebanon front where Hezbollah has promised a response Israel answered with a human-shields accusation, three Hormuz vessel strikes inside 48 hours with 15 ADNOC ships hit since February, Friday transits down to two with no crude at all, seven killed and roughly $16 million of damage at Mocha with the port suspended, oil spills now reaching Oman's coast and Iranian waters near Qeshm, WTI at $82.40 after a +5% week and +33% year with an IEA deficit warning attached, and a 10Y at 4.696% pressing a 19-month high. Pulling the other: VIX within a point of its 52-week low, an index that closed the week only 0.13% lower after a third consecutive higher week, a White House official's statement that the Hormuz territorial claim was a joke, and a Friday tape that absorbed the escalation with a mid-range settle rather than a liquidation. Treat the reopen as a checkpoint to be scored on observed price path, not as a pre-committed direction. The dated calendar checkpoints begin Monday and culminate in the FOMC minutes on Wednesday; the undated ones - the Treasury's Iran package and the exact hour of the negotiating-window lapse - are deliberately absent from the verified calendar because no exact time has been published.
headline: Araghchi says no US-Iran talks are being held at all as June's 60-day negotiating window runs out Monday, and Gharibabadi ties the Hormuz blockade to US acceptance of defeat - Stress 58%, Tail 11% with CME shut, action EA_ON.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from the primary quote page, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, on 397,964 contracts, opening at 30,210.75 and settling inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide with no close pinned to either extreme. NQ sits about 2.7% below its 52-week high of 30,975.50 against a 52-week low of 22,961.50. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, about 2.3% below its 52-week high, completing a third consecutive higher week. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle, several percent off the highs, is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension and pinning near extremes that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency here is not merely low - it is unmeasurable, because nothing has traded for more than nineteen hours.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close, re-verified this hour where it could move). The split in the evidence remains the central fact of this assessment. Equity volatility is calm to the point of complacency: VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60% on the day, inside a 14.18-14.72 range and only 0.87 points above its 52-week low of 13.38 against a 52-week high of 35.30. Rates and energy say the opposite. The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 4.696%, +5.5bp on the day and at the top of a 4.625-4.700% range, pressing the 52-week high of 4.747% set earlier in the week; the 2-year closed at 4.171%, +3.1bp - a curve steepening on long-end inflation aversion rather than a growth scare. WTI stands at $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day, +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and +32.95% on the year; Brent at $88.52, +$1.45 or +1.67%. Trading Economics attributes the move to Treasury Secretary Bessent's promised "unprecedented economic measures" against Iran, the continuing naval blockade of Iranian ports, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery and an IEA warning of the widest 2026 global supply shortfall in five years, partly offset by additional Middle Eastern crude reaching U.S. markets. An index within 2.3% of its high while oil is up a third on the year and the long end presses a 19-month high is a conflicted configuration, and by the risk definition a conflict of that kind belongs in Stress, not in Tail.

GEOPOLITICS (new this hour). The Iran thread changed in kind, not just in degree. Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi posted early Saturday that "This strait will only be opened and closed under Iran's command, and as long as you do not accept the reality of defeat and stop indulging in delusions, Iran will continue to enforce the blockade", adding that the waterway "cannot be seized with a tweet, nor with an aircraft carrier, nor by issuing an order" and, separately, that Hormuz "has been Iranian, is Iranian, and will remain Iranian." This is a response to Trump's statement on Friday at a Nassau County police academy that he would "pretty soon" declare "the Hormuz Strait a territory of the United States" once victory was secured, characterising Iran as "very evil" and defending slightly higher gasoline prices as an acceptable cost of preventing proliferation; a senior White House official has since said Trump was joking, which is a genuine de-escalatory qualifier and is scored as one. The more consequential item is procedural: Araghchi stated early Saturday that "No negotiations have been held between us and the United States at this time" and that Tehran has not decided whether to resume them, while the 60-day window to negotiate final terms - triggered by the memorandum formally signed in June - expires on Monday having seen minimal direct talks. Araghchi's separate position is that the United States continues to violate that memorandum and that until the violations end and are compensated, "the possibility of resuming negotiations does not exist." The physical picture matches the diplomatic one: only two vessels transited the strait on Friday with no visible crude shipments against a 130-140 peacetime daily norm, a bulk carrier was struck by an unknown projectile, and a further ADNOC-linked vessel was hit - the third reported incident inside 48 hours, taking the cumulative ADNOC tally to 15 since February - with oil spills now reaching Oman's coastline and Iranian waters near Qeshm Island. On Lebanon, the position is unchanged from last hour in substance and is important precisely for what has not happened: Hezbollah has condemned the strikes as a "brutal massacre" and an "act of aggressive escalation", accused Netanyahu of escalating "to bolster his domestic political standing", warned that continued attacks would be "met accordingly" and urged Beirut to abandon the "humiliating" negotiations - but no actual Hezbollah retaliatory fire has been reported. The Israeli Prime Minister's office has answered the casualty count with the accusation that Hezbollah deliberately placed civilians inside the compound as "human shields"; the confirmed toll is 11 killed including three children, with 12-19 wounded, and a Hezbollah battalion commander killed in Ansar. In Yemen, the Mocha port director reports "more than 25 missiles" struck the facility, killing seven, causing roughly $16 million in damage and suspending port operations.

SCORING. Tail rises one point to 11%, still deep in the low band. Every ingredient the definition demands - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, price holding near extremes - requires a live tape, and there is none; the last observed tape showed the opposite. The 11% is not a claim about structure but a price for weekend headline discontinuity expressing as a Sunday gap, and it is one point higher than last hour because the diplomatic off-ramp is now confirmed empty rather than merely stalled, with a dated Monday expiry attached. Stress rises two points to 58% (elevated), reflecting a blockade explicitly conditioned on U.S. acceptance of defeat, a negotiating window lapsing into a channel Iran says is not open, a third Hormuz vessel strike inside 48 hours against Friday traffic of two ships and no crude, a Yemeni port shut with seven dead, and spills reaching two coastlines - set against the genuine counterweights of a VIX near its 52-week low, an index that closed the week almost unchanged, no actual Hezbollah retaliation despite the warning, and a White House official walking back the territorial claim as a joke. Confidence is 62% (solid): this hour re-read NQ futures, VIX and both crude benchmarks directly and corroborated the Iranian statements and the window expiry across three independent primaries; the 2-year and 10-year yields and the verified seven-day calendar are carried forward from earlier direct reads, which is legitimate because a Friday close and a set of dated releases cannot change over a weekend. Two fetches were refused with HTTP 403 and were replaced by other primary sources rather than left as gaps. The remaining defect is the unavoidable staleness of the price evidence. Dominant mode is mixed: complacent equity volatility against stressed rates and energy is precisely a mixed regime, not a trend.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout, so the action was EA_ON and the status green in every available slot. Tail held 7-9% across the back half of Friday's U.S. cash session, where the data landed and produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, then printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress traced a clear event arc: 42% at 16:00 UTC easing to 40-41% across the U.S. afternoon, then 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. From 06:00 UTC the weekend escalation sequence lifted the series steadily - Tail to 10% and Stress through 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53%, 54%, 55% and 56% - as the Mocha barrage, the Lebanon strikes, the ADNOC vessel attack, the U.S. territorial claim, Hezbollah's retaliation warning and the state-level condemnations from Salam and Aoun landed one after another with no tape to absorb them. Confidence ran 37-62%, weakest in the hours immediately around the weekly close and improving steadily from 57% to 62% across the weekend halt as each dimension was re-verified hour by hour. The 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August is unavailable because no successful Claude snapshot was published for that hour; those fields are null and no past opinion has been rewritten.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 16:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 15:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly six hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 11% through the remaining Saturday slots, stepping to 12% from 22:00 UTC and to 13% from Sunday morning as the reopen edges into view; those increments reflect accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to hold at 58% through the thin Saturday hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, firming to 59% overnight and to 60% across Sunday midday as the unresolved threads converge on the reopen and on Monday's lapse of the 60-day negotiating window. Confidence drifts from 62% to 55% across the horizon as the last live prints age further without replacement. The material catalyst sits just beyond the horizon: the CME reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which the danger window brackets, and which is now also the last liquid session before that window expires. Inside the horizon the realistic risks are headline-driven - an actual Hezbollah retaliation converting a warning that has so far produced no fire, a further Hormuz vessel strike after the third in 48 hours, an early leak of the Treasury's Iran package, a formal Iranian or U.S. statement on the lapsing memorandum, or any movement on Gharibabadi's blockade-until-defeat condition - each of which would move Stress and the expected gap rather than produce observable one-way structure. The first scheduled checkpoint is Monday's Empire State print at 12:30 UTC; the week's highest-impact dated items are Tuesday's housing and industrial production data, the FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 19 August, Thursday's claims and Philadelphia Fed pair, and Friday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Its highest-impact undated items are the Treasury's Iran package and the precise hour at which the negotiating window lapses, both omitted from the calendar because no exact time has been published. Nvidia's results on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium later that month both fall outside this seven-day window.
